A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ADVICE by the same authors and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–G. Relocated material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original calibration, QA-accuracy, ablation and model-attribution experiments, including additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The training-triplet construction, LM/JSD/margin/sum objectives and ConfTuner integration are unchanged. Explicitly identifying the conditional confidence distributions in Section 4.2 clarifies the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on TriviaQA and evaluate on TriviaQA, MMLU, LogiQA and appendix SciQ results. QA tasks and seen/unseen confidence formats remain unchanged; relocating training examples adds no coverage.

E2.justification: Default, Prompting, Self-Consistency, ConfTuner and the combined ADVICE/ConfTuner variant retain the same participation in corresponding comparisons. The unseen-format and QA-accuracy comparisons also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Both report the same model sizes, training-sample construction, confidence formats, metrics, masking procedures and training settings. No existing protocol is revised and no new experimental protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The loss ablations, answer-masking tests, attention-rollout comparisons, attribution trajectories and hyperparameter sweep already appear in v2. Added discussion of loss combinations and redistributed attribution panels introduce no new tests or analysis evidence.

E5.justification: The main-results caption retains three random seeds and standard deviations, and the attention-rollout comparison retains its t-test significance statement. No uncertainty-reporting practice or run-count information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in v2 Tables 1–6 match v3 Tables 2–7, including calibration, ablation, unseen-format, accuracy, attribution-ranking and SciQ results. The plotted results and attribution images also match; added prose discusses retained evidence.

T1.justification: The confidence-distribution comparisons, loss equations, metric definitions and probing mathematics retain their substance. Section 4.2 explicitly connects existing distribution symbols to their conditional notation without introducing a new definition, assumption or derivation.

C1.justification: The expanded conclusion restates existing claims about calibration, generalization, efficiency and complementary gains with ConfTuner. Its causal answer-dependence claim was already explicit in v2's introduction; the central contribution is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 adds interpretations of the different behavior of JSD and margin-plus-sum ablations. Section 6.3 newly interprets cross-format and OOD performance as transferable confidence rather than in-domain shortcuts. These extend discussion of unchanged results; the substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The appendices retain the same LoRA, optimizer, hardware, data-construction, confidence-mapping and prompt details, together with ConfTuner access information. Training examples and the hard-negative explanation were already available in v2's appendix.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work discussion retain the same cited works and research positioning. No new comparison with prior research or novelty claim is introduced.

P1.justification: v3 adds localized explanations, expands the conclusion and adds acknowledgments while retaining the section sequence. It moves the hard-negative explanation into Section 4.1 and corrects the SciQ cross-reference from an incorrect figure reference to Table 7.

P2.justification: v2's appendix Figure 13 is split into smaller main-text Figures 4 and 10. Appendix Table 7 becomes main-text Table 1 with a revised header and shortened caption. These relocations cause reflow and renumbering without new graphical evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity through explicit distribution notation, additional explanation of existing results and a corrected SciQ reference. Moving examples and attribution evidence into the main discussion improves accessibility, although the smaller, separated attribution panels are harder to compare. The method and empirical support remain unchanged, so the gain is limited.
